item.title: Chip8 IDE with Compose - Overview
item.description: Video games were a large part of how I became interested in computing. The industry started in the 70s and expanded to include computer games as well as console gaming. By the late 90s when I was a teenager, these two worlds overlapped due to console emulation. Thanks to a 56k modem and a small amount of skill, I was introduced to the world of ROMs, Romhacks, Nesticle, Snes9x, and more. While these tools let me play so many pirated copies of games I couldn’t afford on a child’s salary, they also included tools that hinted at how they were written and how the consoles worked. Unfortunately, my skills at the time left me with the understanding that emulation was more “magic” than “advanced technology”.
